Or the input really is 28 rows and one row was lost in rendering... but the message had 27 lines. Hmm, but do is 28 rows — could also be rendering-added row? Less likely.

Actually wait — maybe the message for demo3 input was truncated by the garbler (lost a row), and the true input has 28 rows. Can't know. But now din parsed cleanly: 27 rows × 24, with markers and cluster.

Now the crucial reanalysis: din cluster at rows 20-24, cols 7-11 (cells listed). Markers (non-cluster): (2,21),(9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19),(15,13),(19,19),(22,15),(23,3). Note (23,9),(23,10),(23,11) and (24,11) are cluster cells.

do: 28x24, 9 tiles at TLs [(0,19),(7,6),(8,12),(11,18),(14,11),(18,18),(21,7),(21,13),(22,1)] (previously found). Tile 5x5.

Now find anchor: 9 markers, 9 TLs. Anchor candidates a: implied = TL+a. Score exact matches:
a=(2,2): implied: (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,9),(23,15),(24,3). Matches: (2,21) ✓; (23,9) is a cluster cell ✗; others no.
a=(1,2): implied: (1,21),(8,8),(9,14),(12,20),(15,13),(19,20),(22,9),(22,15),(23,3). Matches: (15,13)✓,(22,15)✓,(23,3)✓. (22,9) cluster ✗.
a=(2,1): (2,20),(9,7),(10,14),(13,19),(16,12),(20,19),(23,8),(23,14),(24,2): matches (9,7)✓,(13,19)✓.
a=(1,1): (1,20),(8,7),(9,13),(12,19),(15,12),(19,20),(22,8),(22,14),(23,2): 0.
a=(3,2): (3,21),(10,8),(11,14),(14,20),(17,13),(21,20),(24,9),(24,15),(25,3): 0? (24,9)? no.
a=(2,3): (2,22),(9,9),(10,17),(13,21),(16,14),(20,21),(23,10),(23,16),(24,4): (23,10) cluster ✗.
a=(1,3): (1,22),(8,9),(9,15),(12,21),(15,14),(19,21),(22,10),(22,16),(23,4): 0.
a=(0,2): (0,21),(7,8),(8,14),(11,20),(14,13),(18,15),(21,9),(21,15),(22,3): (11,20)✓.
a=(2,0): (2,19),(9,6),(10,13),(13,18),(16,11),(20,18),(23,7),(23,13),(24,1): 0.
a=(3,1): (3,20),(10,7),(11,13),(14,19),(17,12),(21,19),(24,8),(24,14),(25,2): 0.
a=(3,3): (3,22),(10,9),(11,15),(14,21),(17,14),(21,21),(24,10),(24,16),(25,4): 0.
a=(4,2): (4,21),(11,8),(12,14),(15,20),(18,13),(22,20),(25,9),(25,15),(26,3): 0.
a=(4,1): (4,20),(11,7),(12,13),(15,19),(18,12),(22,19),(25,8),(25,14),(26,2): 0.
a=(1,0): (1,19),(8,6),(9,12),(12,18),(15,11),(19,17),(22,7),(22,13),(23,1): 0? (22,7) cluster ✗.
a=(2,4): (2,23),(9,10),(10,18),(13,22),(16,15),(20,22),(23,11),(23,17),(24,5): (23,11) cluster ✗.

Best: a=(1,2) with 3 exact matches, a=(2,1) with 2, a=(2,2) with 1. Hmm but none is clean. With 9 pairs, a correct anchor should give 9/9 unless input corrupted. Corruption in din? The din here parsed with all rows 24 tokens — looks clean! But the garbler could still substitute values.

Consider possibility: markers get corrupted: e.g., true markers differ. For a=(2,2), implied markers: (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,9),(23,15),(24,3). Parsed has (2,21),(9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19),(15,13),(19,19),(22,15),(23,3). Offsets (parsed-implied): (9,7)-(9,8)=(0,-1); (10,15)-(10,14)=(0,+1); (13,19)-(13,20)=(0,-1); (22,15)-(23,15)=(-1,0); (23,3)-(24,3)=(-1,0); parsed extras (11,20),(15,13),(19,19); implied (16,13),(20,20) missing. Hmm: parsed (15,13) vs implied (16,13): (15,13) = implied +(-1,0); (19,19) vs (20,20): (-1,-1); (11,20)?? vs implied (13,20): (-2,0)?

Try a=(1,2) mapping: implied (1,21),(8,8),(9,14),(12,20),(15,13),(19,20),(22,9),(22,15),(23,3). Parsed-implied: (2,21)-(1,21)=(+1,0); (9,7)-(8,8)=(+1,-1); (10,15)-(9,14)=(+1,+1); (11,20)-(12,20)=(-1,0); (19,19)-(19,20)=(0,-1); matches 3 exact. Noisy both ways.

Hmm what if BOTH: the anchor is (1,2) AND rows shifted... Let's try model: din rows ≥k shifted by one row (lost row). For a=(2,2): implied true markers (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,9),(23,15),(24,3). If parsed rows ≥k = true rows (r-k mapping: parsed index p ↔ true p for p<k, true p+1 for p≥k... i.e., lost row at index k): parsed marker positions = true positions shifted: parsed (r,c) = true (r,c) if r<k else (r+1,c)? No wait: if the true row k was dropped, then parsed row p (p≥k) = true row p+1. So true (r,c) appears at parsed (r-1,c) for r>k. Implied true markers → parsed coords: (2,21)→(2,21) if k>2; (9,8)→(9,8) if k>9; (10,14)→(10,14) if k>10; (13,20)→(13,20) if k>13; (16,13)→(15,13) if k≤16>15... k∈(15,16]; (20,20)→(19,19)? no, (20,20)→parsed (19,20) if k=16? k≤20 → (19,20). Parsed has (19,19) not (19,20). Hmm ✗. (23,9)→(22,9): parsed (22,9) is cluster ✗.

Try k=16 exactly: markers below row16 unshifted: (2,21)✓,(9,8)? parsed (9,7) ✗. Dead.

Model with column drift per row: too free.

New angle: assume OUTPUT is clean and complete; the input rendering may corrupt but the COUNT of markers should be 9 (kept) or... under removed: 9 markers + cluster; under kept: 8 markers + cluster? With 9 tiles in output: if kept, the cluster tile = original cluster position TL=(21,7) → cluster at rows21-25, cols7-11. Parsed cluster is at rows20-24! If kept, cluster should be at (21,7). Parsed shows (20,7). Off by one row — consistent with a lost row at index ≤20! If a row was lost BEFORE row 20, parsed cluster rows 20-24 = true 21-25 ✓✓. That supports KEPT + a lost row k≤20 in din!

Then true input = 28 rows, parsed rows ≥k shifted +1. True markers = parsed markers with row+1 for r≥k. True markers: for k≤2: all shift: (3,21),(10,7),(11,15),(12,20),(14,19),(16,13),(20,19),(23,15),(24,3). Compare implied from TLs under kept (TL(21,7) excluded): 8 stamps; implied markers TL+a for the 8 other TLs. For a=(2,2): (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,15),(24,3). Hmm compare with shifted parsed (k≤2): (3,21),(10,7),(11,15),(12,20),(14,19),(16,13),(20,19),(23,15),(24,3) — that's 9 markers but kept needs 8. Doesn't fit.

Let's be systematic: enumerate k∈0..26 (lost row index), kept/removed, a∈[-3..5]². Score = exact matches between implied markers TL+a (excluding cluster TL if kept) and shifted parsed markers. Also require implied markers don't hit cluster cells. And the cluster TL consistency: under kept, TL(21,7) must equal parsed cluster TL shifted: parsed cluster at rows20-24 → true rows 20+1=21..25 if k≤20 → TL true = (21,7) ✓ for any k≤20.

Run this search.

Demo-3 input reconstructed cleanly: 27 rows × 24 (markers at (2,21),(9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19),(15,13),(19,19),(22,15),(23,3); cluster rows 20-24 cols 7-11). Output is 28 rows — so a row was likely lost when the input was rendered. Now a systematic search over (lost-row index, kept/removed, anchor) against the 9 exact tile positions:

steps.text:
The search: with a lost row k∈[10,15] and anchor (2,2), 4 exact hits and the rest are corrupted. Anchor (2,2) = CENTER is still the winner (4 hits, best). Wait — but k range 10-15 means markers above k unshifted: hits (2,21) unshifted... hits include (16,13) which is shifted (parsed 15,13 → true 16,13 when k≤15), (23,15) (parsed 22,15→23,15), (24,3) (parsed 23,3→24,3). So markers above k are shifted +1, below unchanged, and center anchor fits with 4/9 exact. The other 5 markers mismatch due to additional local corruption (e.g., col swaps). Note (9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19),(19,19) — shifted versions (10,7),(11,15),(12,20),(14,19),(20,19) vs implied (9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20). Hmm not great, but center anchor confirmed as best by a wide margin? Check second-best scores — all listed are (2,2). So CENTER is confirmed for 5x5.

But center FAILED on test for kept and removed with both g2 and g3! Contradiction. Unless... the test output is BIGGER than input too! Demo3: input 28 rows (true), output 28 rows. Wait — output is 28x24 and true input also 28x24. Test input is 26x24 → output 26x24. Hmm, that's fine.

Wait, actually — what if the output dims = input dims and I've been producing that. Yes.

So what else differs in the test? Tile! Test tile 3x3 from cluster. Anchor (1,1) center — consistent with "floor-center per dim" rule. Failed 4 ways...

Hold on — maybe the failure is the tile content for the TEST. Test cluster: is it a 3x3 tile or 5x5?? The test cluster rows12-14 cols5-7 — that's only 3 rows but cols 5-7 = 3 cols → 3x3 with cells: (12,5)=1,(12,6)=0,(13,5)=0,(13,6)=3,(13,7)=0,(14,5)=9 — 6 non-bg cells in a 3x3 bbox. But WAIT — maybe the bbox is actually bigger! I took bbox of non-bg cells = rows12-14, cols5-7. Demo3 cluster bbox: rows20-24, cols7-11 = 5x5 with 17 non-bg of 25 — includes bg cells INSIDE the bbox. For the test, could the tile be 5x5 spanning rows12-16? If the cluster's true bbox were 5x5 but rendering dropped cells... g2 and g3 both show cluster only rows12-14. A 3x3 tile centered: rows12-14 cols5-7 ✓ consistent.

Alternatively the test tile should be padded to 5x5?? No.

Hmm, wait — maybe markers should remain visible... tried kept.

What about the anchor for the test: center (1,1). TL = marker-(1,1). With g3 markers: (4,11),(7,21),(8,13),(12,14),(13,9),(14,17),(18,6),(21,13),(23,19). Check in-bounds: (23,19)+2=25 rows ✓ cols 19-21 ✓. Wait (7,21): cols 21-23 ✓. All fine.

Attempts 4,5 were exactly g3+center with kept/removed. Failed. Attempts 3,6 g2. Failed. So either test input differs from both renderings, or rule differs.

Since demo3 now CONFIRMS center anchor (2,2) strongly (best by far), maybe test marker set is wrong. The garbler corrupts individual cells. Both g2/g3 renderings might share identical corruption in the marker set beyond (24,x)? Possible: e.g., one marker position wrong in ALL renderings because the corruption is deterministic per message? Actually different renderings had different corruptions, so unlikely shared... but msg2(g2),msg3,msg4(g3),msg5(g3) — could the ORIGINAL message be rendered with the same underlying corruption each time and my extraction differ? Unknown.

Third option: request demos (5 left) to get more rule evidence, esp. with 3x3 tiles to confirm (1,1) anchor. That costs 1 and doesn't solve test input.

Fourth: reconsider rule details — maybe the tile is stamped TRANSPARENTLY (bg cells of tile → keep underlying = bg anyway) — same thing. Or maybe marker cell in output keeps... it's overwritten by tile center (6 in test tile center? test tile center = (13,6)=3; demo3 tile center=(2,2)=7). Fine.

Or maybe output ALSO includes the original markers as 5? In demo3, implied markers (2,21) etc. — check d2 at (2,21): is it 0 or 3? Under kept hypothesis, marker cells outside cluster would remain 0 in output. Let me check d2[(2,21)] etc. That distinguishes kept definitively! Earlier tile-count analysis said removed, but that assumed 9 stamps. Let me directly check d2 at implied marker positions for a=(2,2) with lost row k~12: true markers: (2,21),(9,8)?,(10,14)?,(13,20)?,(16,13),(20,20)?,(23,9)?,(23,15),(24,3). Check d2 values at these — if 0 (bg), markers were removed; if 0 can't tell since bg... the stamp at TL+(2,2) IS the marker position — tile center covers it! So output at marker = tile center color always. Can't distinguish. OK.

Better distinguish kept: under kept, cluster at TL(21,7) — that's consistent with cluster position (shifted by 1 row, k≤20). Both kept/removed fit. Tile count 9 = 9 markers supports removed; but with lost-row corruption the marker count could be 8 with one spurious. Ugh.

Actually wait — recount: removed implies 9 stamps = 9 markers. Kept implies 8 stamps + cluster-as-tile = 9 tiles, 8 markers. Parsed markers = 9. If one parsed marker is spurious (corruption), kept works. Which parsed marker would be spurious? For kept, stamps = TLs minus (21,7). For a=(2,2),k=12: implied markers: (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,15),(24,3) [8]. Parsed shifted markers: (2,21),(10,7),(11,15),(12,20),(14,19),(16,13),(20,19),(23,15),(24,3) [9]. 4 exact. Spurious ones? Either way, center is the anchor.

So the rule is almost certainly: center anchor, tile = cluster bbox. Test failures then stem from wrong test input reading. 4 combos of {g2,g3}×{kept,removed} failed. What else could be wrong in the test reading?

AH WAIT. What if the test input ALSO lost a row?! If the true test grid is 27x24 (or 26 true but rendered 26...) — no, output must equal input dims; if true test input were 27 rows, my submissions of 26-row outputs fail regardless! That's a compelling hypothesis: the test message might have dropped a row of the input! If true input is 27x24, output 27x24. But which row was dropped, and what's in it? If the drop happened in a background-only region, the row is all 6s inserted somewhere... but where? If drop was at the END (row 26 lost) — but g2/g3 both show 26 rows; true 27 rows with last row all bg? Then output = my previous submission padded with a bg row! That's plausible! And with kept variant too (attempt 3 was 26 rows).

Hmm, but is dropping the last row plausible? din (demo3) had 27 vs do 28 — lost row could be anywhere. For the test, we have no output to compare. The loss could be anywhere. If it were mid-grid, the cluster would be split/misaligned — but g2/g3 cluster looks coherent (rows12-14 contiguous, forms a clean 3x3 tile). A lost row inside rows12-14 would break it. Lost row elsewhere shifts markers. So: maybe true test input is 27x24 with an all-bg row inserted at unknown position k, and markers below k shift +1.

But then I can't know k! Unless... corruption in marker positions across renderings can localize k? g2 and g3 differ only at (24,19/20) and row12. If a row were lost between renderings, ALL markers below k would differ — they don't (same in g2/g3). But both renderings could come from the same truncated source.

Alternatively maybe the test truly is 26x24 and something else is wrong.

Let me re-examine: what if the tile in the test is not 3x3 but 5x5 — i.e., the cluster's true bbox is 5x5 (rows12-16 or 10-14) and rendering lost bg... no, bg cells are everywhere; bbox is determined by non-bg cells. Test cluster non-bg cells rows12-14 → bbox 3x3 definitively (unless corruption hid cells).

What if the tile for a 3x3 cluster anchors differently? "floor-center per dim" — for 3x3, center (1,1). Consistent.

What if markers = 5s but some "5"s are actually the tile... all 5s isolated. Fine.

OK here's another thought: maybe I have the demo3 TLs slightly wrong because tile matching required full equality — overlapping stamps? No overlaps found; fine.

Or maybe the rule also KEEPS the markers (adds tile AROUND marker, marker stays as bg under center... center of test tile is 3, so marker cell becomes 3). Yes that's the standard.

Let me look at second-best anchor candidates more carefully to make sure (2,2) is truly the max — the search printed only hits≥3, all (2,2) with 4 hits. (1,2) earlier had 3 hits without shift. So center wins with shift model.

Hmm, let me also check: maybe the shift model k for demo3 is 12ish and there are FIVE corrupted markers — that's a lot. Let me look at the shifted parsed markers vs implied for k=12, a=(2,2):
implied (all 9): (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,9),(23,15),(24,3).
shifted parsed (k=12): (2,21),(9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19),(16,13),(20,19),(23,15),(24,3). Wait parsed rows ≥12 shift: (13,19)→(14,19); (15,13)→(16,13); (19,19)→(20,19); (22,15)→(23,15); (23,3)→(24,3). Cluster also shifts: rows 21-25 → but TL(21,7) cluster = rows 21-25 cols 7-11. Then (23,9) implied marker is INSIDE cluster! Conflict again for a=(2,2)!! TL(21,7)+(2,2)=(23,9) — cluster cell. Under removed, cluster still exists in INPUT. Implied marker (23,9) inside cluster region (rows21-25, cols7-11, cell (23,9)=7 non-bg) — impossible!

Hmm! Unless the cluster in the true input is at a different position — the cluster is the one thing that should NOT be corrupted... The parsed cluster rows 20-24. If k≤20, true cluster rows 21-25 and TL(21,7)+(2,2)=(23,9) lands on cluster cell (23,9)=7. Under kept, TL(21,7) is not a stamp — that's the cluster itself; then stamps = other 8 TLs, and implied markers exclude (23,9). That works! So KEPT + k≤20 + a=(2,2): implied markers (8): (2,21),(9,8),(10,14),(13,20),(16,13),(20,20),(23,15),(24,3). Parsed shifted (k=12): 9 markers incl. those 4 exact: (2,21),(16,13),(23,15),(24,3). Extra parsed: (9,7),(10,15),(11,20),(13,19)→shifted (14,19),(20,19). So 5 extra parsed markers?? That's too many for "one spurious".

Alternatively k such that parsed (11,20)→true (12,20)... For a=(2,2): implied (13,20). parsed (11,20) with k=... if k>11, parsed (11,20) stays (11,20)≠(13,20). ✗.

Honestly the corruption is too messy. Step back.

The strongest structural facts for demo3: 9 exact tiles in output; center anchor has best score (4/9); kept is possible (avoids marker-on-cluster conflict); removed has the (23,9) conflict unless k>20 (then cluster true rows 20-24 unshifted... if k>20, cluster parsed rows20-24 = true 20-24, TL(21,7)? cluster TL true = (20,7) but stamp at (21,7) — mismatch! Under removed, the stamp TL(21,7) needs a marker at (23,9) — inside cluster. Under kept, cluster TL must be (21,7) → needs k≤20. And with k≤20, kept works, removed dead.)

So demo3 says: KEPT + center. But test kept+center failed (both g2 and g3)! AAARGH.

Unless the demo3 "kept" reading is wrong and corruption placed a marker... 

Let me flip: trust test renderings (g3 majority, now 3/4) and center anchor; kept failed; removed failed. What ELSE? The TEST TILE maybe isn't [[1,0,6],[0,3,0],[9,6,6]]! What if the tile in output is not just the bbox but bbox EXTENDED by context — e.g., the demo3 tile 5x5 includes bg cells; the test tile 3x3 also. Fine.

OR: the tile might be MIRRORED/ROTATED per marker based on something (e.g., position parity). Can't detect from demo3 (all 9 stamps same orientation). Hmm.

OR: maybe output = input dims PLUS... test output could be larger? Demo3: input 28(?) output 28 — same. OK.

OR: maybe the cluster stays AND each marker gets a tile AND the output markers... tried.

Let me reconsider whether demo3 supports anchor (1,2) better under some shift. Score (1,2) under shift: run the search printing top per anchor. Let me redo search including kept and printing best score per (dr,dc). The earlier output showed only (2,2) rows with 4 hits ≥3... (1,2) didn't reach 4. So center best.

Given center + both kept/removed failed on test with g2/g3, remaining possibilities:
A) Test input has a lost/extra row (dims wrong). Cheap-ish to test? A submission costs 1; 2 left. Can't scan k.
B) Marker set corrupted beyond renderings' differences.
C) Tile orientation transformed.

For (A): the most likely corruption by analogy with demo3 (where do=28 = true input dims, din=27 rendered) is that the TEST input rendered as 26 rows is actually 27, and output should be 27 rows. Where's the lost row? If k≤... the cluster (rows12-14) looks intact. If lost row k>14, markers below shift. Which marker positions then? True markers: (5,12),(8,22),(9,14),(13,15),(14,10),(15,18),(19,7),(22,14),(24,20)+1 for rows≥k. For the OUTPUT, I'd need k to place stamps... unknown k → can't submit confidently.

Hmm wait, actually — is it possible that the test message I parsed DID have a blank-line structure like di (with blank lines between rows) and I misparsed earlier?? The di blank-line parse gave 27 rows. For the test grid, earlier parses gave 26 rows. Different messages, whatever.

Alternative plan: request a demo (5 left) hoping for a demo with 3x3 tile to confirm anchor AND kept/removed definitively. But corrupt inputs make that hard again... though with TWO clean-ish facts (tile-count exactness in outputs — outputs have been clean!), maybe outputs alone can decide kept/removed: if a demo output has T tiles and the input has M markers + cluster: kept→tiles=M+1? no wait kept→tiles = markers count = T, cluster IS one tile. removed→tiles = markers = T too! Tiles = markers either way. Distinguish via cluster position: if cluster-as-tile appears at its input position (kept) → one TL equals cluster bbox TL. In demo3, cluster parsed TL=(20,7), stamps include (21,7) ≠ (20,7)... unless shift k≤20 makes true cluster TL (21,7) = stamp TL → kept. Ambiguous.

Hmm, but actually think about the size: demo3 tile is 5x5 = cluster bbox 5x5. In the test, cluster bbox is 3x3 → tile 3x3. If the rule were "tile = cluster bbox", sizes vary. OK.

What about "kept" semantics: cluster stays, tiles stamped at markers. Attempt 3/4 did that with center. Failed both g2/g3.

Let me question the test marker list again. Actually, WAIT. Let me recheck: in attempt 3-6, did I use anchor (1,1) meaning TL=marker-(1,1) — yes. For g3 removed (attempt5): TLs (4,11),(7,21),(8,13),(12,14),(13,9),(14,17),(18,6),(21,13),(23,19). Overlap check: (12,14) rows12-14 cols14-16; (13,9) rows13-15 cols9-11 — cluster cols5-7 — no overlap. OK.

And for g2 (attempt 6): last marker (24,19)→TL(23,18).

Hmm hm hm. What if the corruption is in the TEST TILE region? g2 vs g3 differ at row12: g2 has shape cols6-7 (i.e., (12,6)=1,(12,7)=0), g3 has (12,5)=1,(12,6)=0. I used the rendering's tile. The TRUE tile could be different — e.g., true cluster might be [[?,1,0],[0,3,0],[9,?,?]] etc. The tile content matters! If the true cluster differs (corruption moved a cell), ALL stamps are wrong → all 4 attempts fail! 

Can I determine the true tile? The cluster: (12,5)=1,(12,6)=0,(13,5)=0,(13,6)=3,(13,7)=0,(14,5)=9 (g3). g2: (12,6)=1,(12,7)=0, others same. So difference: is row12 "1 0" at cols5-6 or 6-7? For a coherent 3x3 tile... both are coherent. The center (13,6)=3 either way.

Consider a third hypothesis for row12: maybe it's (12,5)=1,(12,6)=0,(12,7)=? or something else entirely (corruption substituted). No way to know.

Options for next submission (2 left). Actually — should I request a demo instead? A demo output is clean; a demo with a 3x3 cluster would give: tile = bbox (testable), anchor for 3x3, kept/removed. But it wouldn't fix the test input corruption. However, if the rule is actually right and the failure is input corruption, more demos don't help either. 

Expected value: submit costs 1, demo costs 1. With 2 submits left: possible remaining variants: (g3 removed center with tile row12 = g2?? mixing), tile transformed (mirror), etc. Too many.

Hmm wait, actually, let me recheck one thing: the demo3 anchor could ALSO be (2,2) with the OTHER pairing where markers map to stamps in different order — no, mapping must be position-based (marker + a = TL).

Let me reconsider: is it possible the anchor is NOT center but the search is fooled? The search maximized hits under a shift model. (2,2) got 4. Check (1,2),(2,1),(0,2) etc. best scores under shift — the output only showed (2,2) for hits≥3... with shift, (1,2) might get 3 but wasn't in top-12? All top entries were 4 hits. Fine, (2,2) unique best. CENTER confirmed.

New idea for the test: maybe the test input ALSO has a LOST ROW, and like demo3, it's rendered 1 row short. Demo3: din 27 rendered, do 28. If the harness message consistently loses exactly one row... test true = 27x24! Where lost? Consider the pattern: in demo3, the lost row was somewhere in rows 10-15 (k∈[10,15] fit; actually hits required k∈{10..15}). Hmm k∈[10,15] — that's suspiciously like... mid-grid. For the test, if k∈[10,15] too?? If k≤12, cluster would shift → cluster true rows 13-15, and markers (5,12),(8,22),(9,14) unshifted, others +1. But the cluster then wouldn't align with my stamping... 

Honestly, maybe the corruption isn't "lost row" — the din might genuinely be 27 rows and do 28 with the OUTPUT including an extra row? No — output dims should equal input dims.

Actually wait, maybe not! What if the output dims = input dims but I misjudged: maybe the true demo3 input IS 27 rows and the do rendering GAINED a row?? Corruption can duplicate. If true input is 27x24 and output 27x24, then do's extra row is corruption and TLs near the bottom shift... this changes anchor analysis! If do has a DUPLICATED row, TLs below the duplication shift.
